events.title: The future emperor Nero is born at Antium
events.description: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, later the emperor Nero, was born at Antium to Agrippina the Younger. Adopted by Claudius, he became emperor at 16 and was the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.
events.html: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, later the emperor Nero, was born at Antium to Agrippina the Younger. Adopted by Claudius, he became emperor at 16 and was the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.

events.title: Belisarius defeats the Vandal king Gelimer at Tricamarum
events.description: West of Carthage, the Byzantine army of Belisarius defeated the Vandal king Gelimer, whose brother Tzazon was killed. Gelimer fled to the mountains and surrendered in 534, ending the Vandal Kingdom and restoring North Africa to the Roman Empire.

events.title: Sergius I is elected pope as a compromise between two rivals
events.description: Sergius I was elected bishop of Rome while two rivals, Paschal and Theodore, were disputing which of them should become pope. His refusal to accept the canons of the Quinisext Council later led Emperor Justinian II to order his arrest.

events.title: Constantine VIII becomes sole emperor after 63 years as co-emperor
events.description: Co-emperor in name since 962, alongside his father Romanos II, Nikephoros II Phokas, John I Tzimiskes and his brother Basil II, Constantine VIII became sole emperor on Basil's death. He ruled alone until 1028.
events.html: Co-emperor in name since 962, alongside his father Romanos II, Nikephoros II Phokas, John I Tzimiskes and his brother Basil II, Constantine VIII became sole emperor on Basil's death. He ruled alone until 1028.

events.title: Jin emperor Wanyan Liang is assassinated by his own officers
events.description: After the Jin defeat by the Southern Song at the Battle of Caishi, officers of the Jurchen emperor Wanyan Liang rebelled and killed him in his camp. His successor posthumously demoted him to the rank of prince.
events.html: After the Jin defeat by the Southern Song at the Battle of Caishi, officers of the Jurchen emperor Wanyan Liang rebelled and killed him in his camp. His successor posthumously demoted him to the rank of prince.

events.title: Stephen the Great defeats Matthias Corvinus at the Battle of Baia
events.description: Stephen the Great, prince of Moldavia, defeated the Hungarian king Matthias Corvinus, who was wounded three times, at Baia. Matthias had invaded Moldavia after Stephen annexed Chilia, a Black Sea fortress and harbour, from Hungarian and Wallachian forces.

events.title: The Bill of Rights is ratified
events.description: Virginia's approval gave the first ten amendments to the US Constitution the required three-quarters of states. They guarantee freedoms of speech, religion, press and assembly, and rights to due process.

events.title: Sitting Bull is killed at Standing Rock
events.description: Lakota leader Sitting Bull, a leader at the victory over Custer at the Little Bighorn, was shot dead by Indian police trying to arrest him. Two weeks later came the massacre at Wounded Knee.
events.html: Lakota leader Sitting Bull, a leader at the victory over Custer at the Little Bighorn, was shot dead by Indian police trying to arrest him. Two weeks later came the massacre at Wounded Knee.

events.title: Gone with the Wind premieres in Atlanta
events.description: The film of Margaret Mitchell's novel premiered at Loew's Grand Theatre in Atlanta. It won eight competitive Academy Awards, and allowing for inflation it remains the highest-grossing film ever.
events.html: The film of Margaret Mitchell's novel premiered at Loew's Grand Theatre in Atlanta. It won eight competitive Academy Awards, and allowing for inflation it remains the highest-grossing film ever.

events.title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa reopens
events.description: After eleven years of closure and stabilisation work, the Leaning Tower of Pisa reopened to visitors. Engineers had reduced its tilt by about 44 centimetres, securing it for centuries.

song: Hindu devotees: Smarthas, Vaishnavas and others
A Sanskrit hymn said to be by the teacher Adi Shankara, telling people to praise God instead of wasting their lives on things that pass.
